questions.text: How doth the Preacher judge all labour of man in Ecclesiastes 1:2?

options.text: It is eternal and can never pass away
Vanity of vanities; all is vanity under the sun
It is continually blessed of God alone
It is the source of all heavenly wisdom

questions.text: What image for the perpetual cycle of nature doth the Preacher use in Ecclesiastes 1:7?

options.text: The wind bloweth toward the south, and whirleth about continually
The stars rise and go down in their appointed celestial course
All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea is not full
The harvest ripeneth in the fields and is gathered year by year

questions.text: What conclusion doth the Preacher reach after beholding all his works and pleasures?

options.text: It was all good and brought enduring profit under the sun
It was all profitable and satisfied the soul with abiding peace
It was the wise man's true reward and nothing was lost of it
All was vanity and vexation of spirit, and there was no profit under the sun

questions.text: What happeneth to the wise man even as to the fool in Ecclesiastes 2:14-16?

options.text: One event happeneth to them all: they die
The same great age and the same poverty in their death
The same open reproach and the same captivity
The same grievous sickness and the same heavy affliction

questions.text: What is declared in Ecclesiastes 3:1 concerning all purpose under the heaven?

options.text: It dependeth upon the changing will of earthly kings
To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose
It faileth continually without heavenly knowledge
It endeth only in vanity and grief under the sun

questions.text: What hath God done concerning the heart of man in Ecclesiastes 3:11?

options.text: He hath caused their heart to rejoice in all earthly riches
He hath hardened their heart against all heavenly instruction
He hath set the world in their heart, so that no man can find it out
He hath established their heart in quiet peace through all time

questions.text: What image doth the Preacher use in Ecclesiastes 4:12 for the strength of companionship?

options.text: A rock in the sea that withstandeth every tempestuous storm
A fruitful tree planted by the waters that never falleth
A brazen shield that turneth away the arrows of the enemy
A threefold cord is not quickly broken

questions.text: What counsel doth the Preacher give concerning a vow in Ecclesiastes 5:4?

options.text: When thou vowest a vow, defer not to pay it
Make vows only in the presence of holy priests
Put off the payment of a vow until prosperity
To make but few words before God

questions.text: What doth Ecclesiastes 5:10 say concerning him that loveth money?

options.text: He shall quickly become rich and have plenty
He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver
He shall find quiet peace in his great abundance
He shall become a generous giver unto the poor

questions.text: With what doth Ecclesiastes 7:1 compare a good name?

options.text: Better than great store of refined gold
Better than sweet noble wine in cup
A good name is better than precious ointment
Better than the honeycomb of the field

questions.text: What counsel doth Ecclesiastes 7:9 give concerning anger?

options.text: Anger is a sign of valour and firmness in the assembly of elders
Anger cleanseth the mind and bringeth hidden righteousness to light
Anger is righteous zeal and is commended by the judges of people
Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in fools

questions.text: Why is a living dog better than a dead lion according to Ecclesiastes 9:4-5?

options.text: For the living know that they shall die, and to him that is joined there is hope
Because the dog is faithful and followeth his master, but the lion is wild
Because the lion loseth his great strength in death and no man feareth him
Because the dog is useful in the house, but the dead lion profiteth nothing

questions.text: What doth the Preacher relate in Ecclesiastes 9:14-15 concerning a little city?

options.text: A valiant captain defended it with soldiers, yet he fell before the gates
A poor wise man by his wisdom delivered the city, yet no man remembered him
The elders paid much gold unto the king, yet the city was utterly ruined
The citizens built a high wall round about, yet the enemy breached the towers

questions.text: What causeth the ointment of the apothecary to stink in Ecclesiastes 10:1?

options.text: Foul river water
The scorching sun
Dead flies cause it
An excess of salt

questions.text: What counsel is given in Ecclesiastes 11:1?

options.text: Sow thy seed only upon fertile soil, so shalt thou reap an abundant harvest
Hide thy corn from the eyes of strangers, that thou mayest survive famine
Bestow thy goods only upon the righteous, so shalt thou have blessing in house
Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days

questions.text: Whom shouldest thou remember in the days of thy youth according to Ecclesiastes 12:1?

options.text: Remember now thy Creator, while the evil days come not
The holy statutes of Moses, that thy days may be prolonged
The ancient wisdom of the elders who walked before God
The sacred covenant made with thy fathers in the wilderness

questions.text: What is the conclusion of the whole matter according to Ecclesiastes 12:13?

options.text: To build cities and establish just laws for all future generations
Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man
To study ancient wisdom and teach understanding unto simple youth
To offer morning and evening sacrifices upon the altar in Jerusalem

questions.text: Who identifieth himself as the speaker of the book in Ecclesiastes 1:1?

options.text: Moses, the servant of the LORD, who received the law
Isaiah the son of Amoz, who saw the word
The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem
Ahijah the Shilonite, who foretold the kingdom unto Jeroboam

questions.text: What followeth upon much wisdom according to Ecclesiastes 1:18?

options.text: Great peace and deep rest for the wise man and his house
Great power and high honour among the princes of the land
Great riches and a long life in prosperity
For in much wisdom is much grief: and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow

questions.text: With what doth Ecclesiastes 7:6 compare the laughter of the fool?

options.text: As the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool
As the loud croaking of frogs in the marshes when darkness falleth
As the hooting of desert owls among the deserted ruins of the city
As the roaring of wild beasts of the wilderness that seek after prey

questions.text: What counsel doth Ecclesiastes 11:2 give in view of coming evil upon the earth?

options.text: Lay up secret storehouses of silver against the days of famine
Give a portion to seven, and also to eight, for coming evil
Flee into the high mountain fortresses before the storm breaketh
Rely only upon thine own kindred and put no confidence in strangers

questions.text: How doth Ecclesiastes 12:3 describe old age in figurative language?

options.text: The trees wither and the fruit falleth from the bough
The ship sinketh and the sails are rent in the storm
The keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow
The mountains sink down and the valleys are filled up

questions.text: What happeneth at death according to Ecclesiastes 12:7?

options.text: The body sleepeth in the sepulchre, and the soul resteth in silence
The flesh perisheth in the earth, and the spirit wandereth in darkness
The dust returneth to ashes, and the memory fadeth like a morning mist
The dust shall return to the earth, and the spirit unto God who gave it

questions.text: What doth Ecclesiastes 12:12 say concerning the making of books?

options.text: Of making many books there is no end
The making of books bringeth great fame
The making of books increaseth all wisdom
The making of books delighteth the monarch

questions.text: What shall happen according to Ecclesiastes 12:14?

options.text: The earth shall pass away and a new heaven shall be created in glory
God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing
The names of all the wicked shall be blotted out of remembrance
The righteous shall inherit the kingdoms of the earth for evermore

questions.text: What is good for man according to Ecclesiastes 2:24?

options.text: That he should eat and drink, and make his soul enjoy good in his labour
That he should lay up treasures of silver and be secure from all want
That he should rule over his neighbours and be a renowned prince in land
That he should study ancient lore and abstain from all worldly pleasure

questions.text: Unto what purpose doth God work according to Ecclesiastes 3:14?

options.text: That the nations may acknowledge his boundless mighty power
God doeth it, that men should fear before him in reverence
That the righteous may receive great riches upon the earth
That the counsel of the ungodly rulers may be brought to nought

questions.text: What did the Preacher behold with grief in Ecclesiastes 4:1?

options.text: The ungodly rulers rejoicing in their great worldly palaces
The temples of false gods erected upon the high mountains
The tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter
The faithful priests neglected while the people went astray

questions.text: Who is better than an old and foolish king according to Ecclesiastes 4:13?

options.text: A wealthy merchant
A valiant soldier
A prudent magistrate
Better is a poor and a wise child

questions.text: What counsel is given in Ecclesiastes 5:2 concerning speaking before God?

options.text: Be not rash with thy mouth: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth
Pray with a loud voice in the market that men may see thy devoutness
Speak only within the temple walls, for there only doth the LORD hear
Repeat thy words three times in prayer that they may prevail with God

questions.text: What grievous evil is described in Ecclesiastes 6:1-2?

options.text: A man buildeth a house, but a hostile army consumeth it with fire
God giveth riches, yet not power to eat thereof, but a stranger eateth it
A ruler gathereth silver and gold, but his unfaithful servants steal it
A wise man planteth a vineyard, but a severe drought destroyeth the crop

questions.text: Who is better off than a man whose soul is NOT filled with good in Ecclesiastes 6:3?

options.text: A poor hired labourer
A wandering stranger
An untimely birth is better
An aged blind beggar

questions.text: What is better according to Ecclesiastes 6:9?

options.text: To pursue every distant desire rather than be content with little
To lay up large storehouses of grain rather than eat daily bread
To seek after the wealth of strangers rather than dwell in peace
Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire

questions.text: What is said concerning the word of a king in Ecclesiastes 8:4?

options.text: Where the word of a king is, there is power: who may say, What doest thou?
In his word is righteous judgment, and all his people obey with gladness
In his word is tender mercy, and the destitute find a sure refuge in him
In his word is deceitful vanity, and no wise counsellor relieth upon it

questions.text: Why is the heart of men fully set in them to do evil in Ecclesiastes 8:11?

options.text: Because they no longer believe the holy statutes of the ancient law
Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily
Because the magistrates in the gate take bribes from violent oppressors
Because no man regardeth the words and warnings of the holy prophets

questions.text: What assurance doth the Preacher maintain in Ecclesiastes 8:12?

options.text: All the children of men receive the same earthly reward in life
Abundance of worldly riches is the sure token of divine favour
It shall be well with them that fear God, which fear before him
Man directeth his own destiny by the strength of his understanding

questions.text: What counsel doth Ecclesiastes 9:10 give?

options.text: Wait until others determine the matter, and then act cautiously
Defer thy work until old age, when thou art grown more prudent
Avoid manual labour and seek after light easy occupations in life
Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might

questions.text: What is said concerning the heart of the wise and the fool in Ecclesiastes 10:2?

options.text: A wise man’s heart is at his right hand; but a fool’s heart at his left
The wise man walketh upon the mountains, but the fool in the valleys
The wise man keepeth silence in assembly, but the fool talketh much
The wise man spareth his bread, but the fool consumeth all his goods

questions.text: Over what doth the Preacher pronounce woe in Ecclesiastes 10:16?

options.text: Over a land without soldiers, whose watchmen sleep and keep no guard
Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and thy princes eat in morning
Over a conquered country that payeth heavy tribute unto foreign kings
Over a barren land without harvest, whose judges pervert the righteous cause

questions.text: What counsel is given to the sower in Ecclesiastes 11:6?

options.text: To sow only under a clear sky and wait patiently for the rainy season
To flee from the field whenever dark clouds begin to gather in heaven
In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand
To sow only half of the grain and reserve the rest against famine
